mechanism_narrative: A high and rising FEDFUNDS rate indicates tighter monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% in 3 months but SPX 20-day returns remain positive in >50% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200 thousand units signals weaker demand in the housing sector, which ripples through the broader economy and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST falls below 1200 but SPX 60-day returns are positive in >40% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by >0.2% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) does not increase, it signals labor market weakness that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises >0.2% without PAYEMS growth but SPX 20-day returns are positive >50% of the time, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in industrial production (INDPRO) growth below 2% year-over-year during a late-cycle expansion signals supply chain constraints and reduced corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is below 2% YoY but SPX 60-day returns are positive >40% of the time, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates tight monetary conditions that reduce corporate investment and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS >4.5 but SPX 20-day returns are positive >50% of the time, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Real consumer spending (RSAFS) increasing by >5% month-over-month signals strong demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases >5% MoM but SPX 5-day returns are negative >30% of the time, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 4.5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth is below 100k month-over-month, it signals a weak labor market that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE >4.5 and PAYEMS growth <100k but SPX 20-day returns are positive >50% of the time, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by >5% year-over-year signals strong supply chain activity, which boosts corporate profitability and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth >5% YoY but SPX 60-day returns are negative >40% of the time, this hypothesis is rejected.
